facts.statement: The type species Albinykus baatar was named by Nesbitt, Clarke, Turner, and Norell in 2011.
facts.quote: The type species, A. baatar, was named by Sterling J. Nesbitt, Julia A. Clarke, Alan H. Turner and Mark A. Norell in 2011.

facts.statement: Fossils of Albinykus have been found in the Santonian-aged Javkhlant Formation in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.
facts.quote: whose fossils have been found in the Late Cretaceous-aged (Santonian) Javkhlant Formation in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Albinykus weighed under 1 kg, making it one of the smallest alvarezsaurids and among the smallest non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Estimated at under 1 kg in weight, Albinykus was one of the smallest alvarezsaurs and among the smallest non avian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Albinykus is distinguished by the complete fusion of its tarsals to other leg bones, a feature not seen in other alvarezsaurids.
facts.quote: One distinguishing feature of Albinykus not seen in other alvarezsaurids is the complete fusion of the tarsals to other bones of the leg

facts.statement: The sitting posture of the Albinykus holotype is similar to that of birds, indicating a close relationship between non-avian maniraptoran dinosaurs and birds.
facts.quote: This posture is similar to that of birds, an indication of the close relationship between nonavian maniraptoran dinosaurs and birds.

facts.statement: Scientists are unsure how the Albinykus holotype died in its preserved position, though it is possible it suffocated under sand.
facts.quote: Scientists are unsure about how the dinosaur died to keep it in the position it was in but it is possible Albinykus suffocated under sand.

facts.statement: The genus Albinykus was established by Nesbitt et al. in 2011.
Albinykus belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae.
Albinykus is classified within the suborder Theropoda.
Albinykus lived from the Santonian to the Campanian stages, between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)
